proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the hospitalization process has dynamics not well-approximated by a fixed lag (e.g., variable lag or admission-duration effects), delayed_I may misalign peak timing and distort amplitude.
proposals.rationale: High peakiness and high rate scale suggest sharp seasonal waves; SEIRS supports waning immunity/seasonal recurrence while fractional dynamics can flexibly capture heavy-tailed rise/decay. delayed_I with 2-week lag matches the stated hospitalization-lag semantics without adding an explicit H compartment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is longer (or varies over the season), a 1-week delay can shift peaks early and bias inferred growth/decline shape.
proposals.rationale: A more parsimonious alternative lag for admissions; keeps the same flexible SEIRS fractional backbone while allowing earlier alignment if the observed hospitalization peak is closer to infection incidence in this age group.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If reinfection/waning immunity materially affects late-season dynamics, SEIR may underfit secondary bumps or prolonged tails.
proposals.rationale: If the 31-week training window largely covers a single dominant wave, SEIR can be sufficient and more identifiable than SEIRS while still allowing fractional dynamics for sharp peaks; delayed_I encodes the admissions lag.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H-related parameters (admission rate, length of stay/exit) may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, leading to unstable forecasts or compensatory parameter tradeoffs.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the target semantics (hospitalization rate) to an explicit H compartment, avoiding reliance on a fixed lag proxy. Non-fractional keeps the template parsimonious given short series and identifiability concerns.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the surveillance signal is closer to pure admissions (H only) or pure incidence proxy (I), the mixed observation can blur peak sharpness and misattribute dynamics between I and H.
proposals.rationale: If reported hospitalization rates reflect a mixture of incident admissions and ongoing hospitalized burden (or coding/reporting blends), observing I+H can be a robust compromise while retaining mechanistic hospitalization structure.
